```text
Wave 1:  T1 Native atomic batch persistence     T4 Browser import API
                 |                                      |

T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T6
T4 -> T5 -------> T6

the backend chain because it consumes T2's error and summary types. T6 begins
only when both tracks are complete.

- Outcome: `EventService` can create multiple ordinary or recurring native
  events and their occurrence exceptions as one authorized, audited transaction.
- Depends on: none
- Scope: `backend/src/event.rs`; initial batch-persistence cases in
  `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Add the approved `EventCreateBatch`, item, exception, recurrence-key,
  and result types; implement `EventService::create_batch`; reuse existing event
  validation, recurrence validation, authorization, audit, CalDAV change, and
  notification-replanner helpers; add focused service tests for atomic rollback,
  exception persistence, side-effect counts, and native editability.
- Out of scope: ICS parsing or UID grouping, HTTP routes, parser error mapping,
  rate-limit classification, frontend work.
- Acceptance: A valid mixed batch commits all top-level events and exceptions;
  invalid input or a database failure commits none; authorization is checked as
  `CreateEvent`; every top-level row has one create audit and CalDAV change;
  imported-style rows have no external mapping and remain editable; notification
  replanning occurs only after commit.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked --test ics_import ics_import_batch`
- Handoff: Stable batch input/result types and proven transactional semantics for
  the ICS coordinator; record exact type names if implementation-required Rust
  adjustments preserve the approved meanings.

## T2 — Convert an ICS file into a native event batch

- Outcome: Bounded valid ICS bytes become native event batches with preserved
  standalone, all-day, timed, recurrence-exclusion, and detached-override
  semantics.
- Depends on: T1
- Scope: new `backend/src/ics_import.rs`, `backend/src/lib.rs`, recurrence and
  parser-limit cases in `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Add `IcsImportService`, import constants, summary, and errors; invoke
  the existing parser with the 1,000-event policy; normalize status and timing;
  group components by UID; attach `EXDATE` and `RECURRENCE-ID` values; reject
  orphan, mismatched, conflicting, unknown-status, malformed, duplicate, and
  over-limit input before persistence; delegate once to `create_batch`; export
  the module.
- Out of scope: HTTP body/media-type handling, route mounting, rate limiting,
  browser API or UI, changes to external-feed ingestion or the generic parser.
- Acceptance: Timed and all-day standalone events import with correct fields;
  a recurring master stores deletions and replacements under the correct keys;
  every semantic or parser failure maps to the approved error category and
  leaves all persistence tables unchanged; re-import creates another editable
  native copy; summary counts top-level events separately from exceptions.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked --test ics_import ics_import_service`
- Handoff: Callable `IcsImportService::import`, stable summary/error contract,
  content-free failure categories, and tested constants for T3.

## T3 — Expose the authenticated, limited import endpoint

- Outcome: Authorized callers can POST raw `text/calendar` bytes and receive the
  approved summary or stable safe error codes through the production router.
- Depends on: T2
- Scope: `backend/src/http.rs`, `backend/src/rate_limiter.rs`, HTTP and role cases
  in `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Mount and implement `POST
  /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics`; verify media type and non-empty
  body; call `IcsImportService`; map errors; emit content-free structured timing
  logs; classify the route as Standard write rate; add authenticated role,
  response-envelope, media-type, 1 MiB limit, and classifier tests.
- Out of scope: service conversion rules, database schema, frontend behavior,
  application-state or router-builder signature expansion.
- Acceptance: Owner, manager, and editor receive 201 for valid input; viewer,
  free/busy viewer, and unrelated caller receive non-enumerating 404; malformed
  and limit failures expose only their stable codes; incorrect media type and
  empty input are 400; oversized input is 413; the route is Standard-rate
  limited; logs contain no calendar content, UID, filename, title, description,
  or location.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked ics_import`
- Handoff: Final backend endpoint contract and complete integration-test evidence
  for the browser and E2E packets.

## T4 — Add the typed browser import API

- Outcome: Frontend callers can upload a `File` as raw calendar content and
  receive typed counts or a safe typed failure code.
- Depends on: none
- Scope: `frontend/src/calendar/api.ts`, `frontend/src/calendar/api.test.ts`
- Changes: Add `IcsImportSummary`, error-code type,
  `IcsImportApiError`, and `importIcs`; send the `File` body with the approved
  media type; parse only `error.code`; fall back safely for malformed or unknown
  error responses; add focused request/response tests.
- Out of scope: Dialog state, card permissions, file prevalidation, styling,
  backend implementation.
- Acceptance: The client uses the exact approved route, method, content type, and
  unmodified `File` body; successful counts are returned; recognized codes are
  typed; unknown bodies never surface server-provided text.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir frontend test -- api.test.ts`
- Handoff: Stable `importIcs` function, summary, and safe error class for T5.

## T5 — Deliver the accessible calendar import flow

- Outcome: Owners, managers, and editors can select, validate, upload, and
  acknowledge an ICS import from an active calendar card.
- Depends on: T4
- Scope: `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.tsx`,
  `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.css`,
  `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.test.tsx`
- Changes: Add the event-creation permission helper and per-card import action;
  implement the import dialog and its file-size/extension validation, pending,
  success, safe-error, Escape, focus, and access-change behavior; style it using
  existing calendar-dialog conventions; add all approved component tests.
- Out of scope: Backend changes, event-list refresh mechanics, calendar creation
  during import, preview or event selection, E2E fixture.
- Acceptance: Only active detail-access owner/manager/editor cards show Import;
  editors gain no management controls; invalid local files make no request;
  a valid file submits once; all pending controls are safe; success shows the
  returned count until acknowledgement; stable failure codes show actionable
  copy without backend text; access denial refreshes calendars; Escape and close
  restore focus to the correct card.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir frontend test -- CalendarManagement.test.tsx`
- Handoff: Completed visible flow and selectors/accessibility names needed by the
  E2E packet.

## T6 — Prove the integrated user journey and document it

- Outcome: A browser-level test proves a real ICS file becomes editable native
  events, and public project documentation describes the new capability.
- Depends on: T3, T5
- Scope: new `e2e/support/import.ics`,
  `e2e/tests/desktop-mvp.spec.ts`, `README.md`, final integrated verification
- Changes: Add the deterministic two-event fixture; drive the visible import
  dialog; assert the success count; verify both events through the API as native
  and writable; update the README feature list and API overview; run focused and
  full relevant checks and fix only regressions caused by this feature.
- Out of scope: Expanding import behavior, deduplication, provider connections,
  external-feed changes, unrelated cleanup or pre-existing failures.
- Acceptance: The desktop E2E flow imports one timed and one all-day event and
  proves they are not external/read-only; README clearly distinguishes one-time
  import from feed subscription; backend and frontend suites, formatting,
  linting, typechecking, build, and the focused E2E test pass together.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir e2e test -- desktop-mvp.spec.ts --project=desktop`
- Handoff: Final test evidence, any environment-specific E2E notes, and confirmation
  that all six packet acceptance conditions pass together.

### T1

- One outcome and one seam: native batch persistence.
- Binary proof: commit-all/rollback-all plus side-effect assertions.
- Lands working without exposing an unused route.

### T2

- One outcome and one uncertain boundary: normalized ICS to native batch.

# Product: ICS file import

## Problem

People moving to Happening, or receiving a calendar export from another service,
cannot bring that file into a Happening calendar. Happening can subscribe to a
remote ICS URL, but those events remain read-only and depend on the remote feed.
For a migration or one-off transfer, people need to upload an `.ics` file and
continue managing the imported events in Happening.

## Success criterion

At least 95% of imports of valid, supported `.ics` files containing up to 1,000
events complete successfully and show the imported events in the selected
calendar, measured by an import attempt followed by a successful completion
result in product telemetry during the first four weeks after launch.

## Announcement

calendar you can edit, select the file, and Happening will add its supported

  `NormalizedCalendar` / `NormalizedEvent` values.

- `IcsParserLimits` provides bounded component, event, text, and recurrence
  parsing. Its default event limit is 500, so import will use a dedicated limit
  of 1,000 events to match the approved product criterion.
- Parser failures already distinguish malformed input, invalid events, exceeded
  limits, and duplicate `(UID, RECURRENCE-ID)` components without exposing file
  contents.

### Event persistence and authorization

- `backend/src/event.rs` owns native event creation, `CreateEvent`
  authorization, recurrence validation, event audit records, CalDAV change
  records, and notification replanning.
- `CalendarAction::CreateEvent` permits owners, managers, and editors, while
  viewers and free/busy viewers are denied. Inaccessible resources are returned
  as not found to avoid resource enumeration.
- Native events live in `events`; recurring-series overrides and exclusions live
  in `event_recurrence_exceptions`.
- External feed ingestion in `backend/src/external_feed.rs` is not a suitable
  write path. It creates `external_event_mapping` rows, makes events read-only,
  and reconciles them on later refreshes.

### HTTP and browser UI

- Authenticated calendar and event routes are assembled in
  `backend/src/http.rs`. All requests already have a 1 MiB body limit, session
  middleware, origin protection, secure response headers, request IDs, and
  optional per-user write-rate limiting.
- `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.tsx` renders one card per calendar.
  Its existing management actions are limited to owners and managers; import
  needs a separate “can create events” check that also includes editors.
- `frontend/src/calendar/api.ts` is the browser API boundary and already maps
  access-changing responses consistently.

## Boundary and ownership

Add `backend/src/ics_import.rs` as the application-level import coordinator. It
owns the import policy and conversion from normalized ICS components into a
native-event batch, but does not own HTTP extraction or generic ICS parsing.

Extend `EventService` with one atomic batch-create operation for already
validated native events and recurrence exceptions. That operation remains the
single owner of native event authorization and persistence invariants, including
audit, CalDAV change tracking, and notification replanning. Single-event create
continues unchanged.

This split prevents the HTTP handler from writing SQL and prevents the import
coordinator from using the external-feed mapping model.

## Entry point and contract

Add one authenticated endpoint:

```text
POST /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics
Content-Type: text/calendar; charset=utf-8

<raw .ics bytes>
```

Success returns `201 Created`:

```json

  "imported_events": 12,
  "imported_exceptions": 2
}
```

`imported_events` counts newly created top-level native events. Detached
recurrence overrides and excluded occurrences are reported separately and do
not inflate the user-facing “events added” count.

The endpoint accepts a raw body rather than `multipart/form-data`. The browser
already has the filename for validation and sends `File` bytes directly; the
server needs only bounded calendar content. This avoids a new multipart parser
and boundary overhead. The existing application body limit caps the request at
1 MiB before parsing.

Expected failures use the standard JSON error envelope with stable codes:

- `invalid_calendar_file` for malformed UTF-8, malformed calendar structure,
  invalid event values, duplicate components, or an unsupported recurrence
  relationship;
- `calendar_import_limit_exceeded` when parser limits are exceeded;
- `404` for a missing calendar or insufficient `CreateEvent` permission;
- `413` from the existing body limiter for a body larger than 1 MiB;
- `429` from the standard write-rate limiter.

The route belongs to the standard event-write rate-limit tier.

No migration or import-tracking table is required. Re-imports intentionally
create new native rows per the approved product behavior.

One `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction will:

1. read the actor's `calendar_acl` role and authorize `CreateEvent`;
2. insert one `events` row for each standalone event or recurrence master;
3. insert `event_recurrence_exceptions` rows for each master `EXDATE` and each
   supported detached `RECURRENCE-ID` override;
4. insert an `event_audit` creation record for each top-level event;
5. record a CalDAV `created` change for each top-level event;
6. commit once.

Any parsing, relationship, validation, authorization, or database failure rolls
the transaction back, leaving the destination calendar unchanged. After commit,
notification replanning is queued once for every created top-level event.

ICS UIDs are used only to assemble masters and detached instances within the
uploaded file. They are not persisted for matching because re-import deduplication
is explicitly out of scope.

## Recurrence mapping

- A component without `RECURRENCE-ID` is a top-level event. Its supported
  `RRULE` is stored on the native event after existing recurrence validation.
- Each `EXDATE` on a recurring master becomes a deleted recurrence exception.
- A component with `RECURRENCE-ID` must refer to exactly one recurring master
  with the same UID in the same file. It becomes a non-deleted exception whose
  timing and fields come from the detached component.
- Orphan detached instances, detached instances for non-recurring masters,
  mismatched timed/all-day recurrence identifiers, conflicting exception keys,
  and unsupported recurrence rules reject the entire import.
- Multiple ordinary components with different UIDs are independent top-level
  events. The existing parser rejects duplicate `(UID, RECURRENCE-ID)` keys.

preserves the approved atomic-import promise.

2. The frontend rejects a missing file, a non-`.ics` filename, or a file over

3. The HTTP handler verifies the media type, reads the bounded body, requires
   UTF-8, and calls `IcsImportService` with actor and calendar identifiers.
4. The coordinator parses with import-specific limits, assembles recurrence
   groups, converts them into native batch inputs, and delegates to
   `EventService`.
5. `EventService` authorizes and persists the complete batch atomically, commits,
   then schedules notification replanning.
6. The API returns counts and emits a structured success log containing only the
   actor ID, calendar ID, counts, byte size, and duration—never event content or
   the local filename.
7. The dialog shows “N events imported” and closes on acknowledgement. The next
   calendar-view load reads the new native events through the existing event API.

- Add an import icon/action to each active calendar card where `role` is owner,
  manager, or editor and detail access is present.
- The dialog identifies the destination calendar, provides one `.ics` file
  input, states the 1 MiB / 1,000-event limits, and has Cancel / Import actions.
- Import is disabled until a file is selected and while a request is active.
- On success, the dialog presents the returned event count. On failure, it maps
  stable API codes to actionable messages and retains the selected destination.
- Archived calendars and read-only calendars do not expose the action.
- Keyboard focus returns to the triggering card action after the dialog closes,
  following the existing sharing-dialog pattern.

No external system is contacted. The file travels from the person's browser to
the existing Happening API and is not stored as a blob.

No new environment variables are required. Limits are code-level constants:

- request/file bytes: 1 MiB (aligned with `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES`);
- parsed VEVENT components: 1,000;
- existing per-component text, size, and recurrence-value bounds remain in
  force, with the component ceiling raised only as needed to accommodate the
  1,000-event contract.

- Emit structured `ics_import_succeeded` and `ics_import_failed` events with
  stable reason codes so the product success criterion can be measured.
- Do not log calendar contents, titles, descriptions, locations, UIDs, file
  bytes, or local filenames.
- Database errors remain internal; client errors disclose only the stable import
  category.

## Architectural risks

- Recurrence conversion is the highest-risk boundary because ICS detached
  instances must map correctly onto the existing native exception schema.
- A 1,000-event transaction can hold SQLite's writer lock long enough to affect
  concurrent writes. All parsing and grouping therefore happens before opening
  the transaction, and the transaction performs only validation queries and
  inserts.
- Audit, CalDAV change, and notification side effects can drift from normal event
  creation if batch persistence duplicates those rules. The batch operation must
  share the existing helper functions and tests must compare imported native
  events with ordinarily created ones.

    event_service: EventService,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct IcsImportSummary {
    pub imported_events: usize,
    pub imported_exceptions: usize,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum IcsImportError {
    InvalidCalendar,
    LimitExceeded,
    NotFound,
    Database(sqlx::Error),
}

impl IcsImportService {
    pub fn new(event_service: EventService) -> Self;

    pub async fn import(
        &self,
        actor_user_id: i64,
        is_superadmin: bool,
        calendar_id: i64,
        bytes: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<IcsImportSummary, IcsImportError>;
}
```

    pub events: Vec<EventCreateItem>,

    pub event: EventMutation,
    pub recurrence_rule: Option<String>,
    pub exceptions: Vec<EventCreateException>,

    pub recurrence: EventRecurrenceKey,
